subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw replace the shipped `.deleted.*`/`.reset.*` session archive convention and retention deletion behavior with a permanent archive naming or directory model, and what migration/purge policy should existing users get?
rationale: This changes shipped filenames, cleanup semantics, disk-budget behavior, and downstream tooling expectations, so code inspection can prove the current behavior but cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Adopt archive terminology with migration
options.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind an explicit documented retention setting.

options.title: Keep behavior and clarify docs
options.body: Leave current suffixes and cleanup behavior intact, but document that `.deleted.*` means detached until retention removes it.

options.title: Split policy from terminology
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/80263 for naming/config clarity and track the no-physical-delete policy as a separate data durability decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt archive terminology with migration
recommendation.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind an explicit documented retention setting.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session product work and current session docs make this the best available owner for choosing the user-facing lifecycle contract.
